questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Living in another city for an extended period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything is in French. Besides that, it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction week is good. You should go to the free French courses before and during your exchange. There you will meet other Erasmus students. Together you will figure it all out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne can provide housing in the Cité. Although you have to pay a fee.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchens were available for all floors in the house I was living in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Depends on which house in the Cité you live in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you arrive you find out which courses are available for the semester. You cannot depend on any information you found earlier. Some courses might have been cancelled. You have one month to figure it all out. After that you cannot change courses anymore.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus team and especially Laetitia helped me out a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses in English in Political Science were cancelled. I had to take a French course and I was extraordinarily allowed to take two courses in English in Economics and one in English in History. So I would not say that I was too successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress. Be proactive in the first month. You are not going to get the courses that you expected before arrival and you are probably going to have some courses in French. Know that everything is going to be all right. All Erasmus students are experiencing the same as you. The Erasmus team at Sorbonne will help you out. Especially if you go to their office.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Depends on the professor. Some courses were stimulating, others were not.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Presentations, learning by heart and exams written in hand. In some courses there might be space for discussion, in others the lecturer speaks and you listen and take notes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Grands débats postcoloniaux (French, Master, Political Science)
France and the EU (English, Master, Political Science)
Issues of Climate Change (English, Master, Political Science)
From the New Deal to the New Right: Political Cultures in the 20th century United States (English, Bachelor, History)
Resources and Climate Change (English, Bachelor, Economics)
International Monetary Economics (English, Bachelor, Economics)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you speak French I would recommend 'Grands débats postcoloniaux'. The professors are really passionated and the discussions are stimulating. I would also recommend 'France and the EU'. Again, because the professor is passionated and the class discussions are stimulating.

questions.answer: A monthly RER-pass is around 600 DKK. I would recommend renting a bike. That way you are going to see the city more.

questions.answer: Groceries are more expensive than I expected.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't do any so I don't know.

questions.answer: I know sports activities were available. But I didn't try it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know as I didn't try any of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out in the city with a book.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Learn some French phrases. It is going to make it all a lot easier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everybody being such enjoyers of life. It is going to rub off on you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress with the registration process. It is going to be all right.
Accept that you live in another country and that things are different. Try to embrace the difference.
Enjoy. You are abroad. Suck it all in.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the free French courses provided by Sorbonne.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Paris at my own pace.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The stress I experienced in the beginning in relation to all the difficulty with the courses. Don't be like me. You are going to figure it all out eventually.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
